threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers by their shocked faces at the prices in the local butcher. It’s like they think they’re at a fancy restaurant.
Last night, saw a guy trying to negotiate with a pigeon for his burger on the 35. Pigeons definitely have better taste than some night bus riders.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting at Tempelhofer Feld, I watched a kid flying a kite with their dog chasing it—no stress, just pure Neukölln vibes. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find spontaneous raves in abandoned buildings, as locals break out their decks and dance under the remnants of the past.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they navigate the BART delays. They plan their days around it, while newbies just shrug and wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 at 7th and Market, and a guy serenaded the whole bus with Frank Sinatra. Everyone was stuck in traffic but smiling. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just a pretty plaza, but it’s the side streets with their quirky shops and local bars that truly breathe life into this neighborhood.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with the metro map, missing the direct lines while staring in confusion at the station names.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver yells at you for not having your Oyster card ready. We know that confusion well.
Saw a guy on the night bus last week, he was drumming on his backpack like it was a bongo. Didn't miss a beat even when we hit that pothole!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade on the corner, while their mom haggled over a bike in broken German. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, the kebab shops are open at all hours, but it’s the breakfast döner at 6 AM that hits different—crispy and surprisingly fresh.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re local when you can spot the tourists taking selfies with the murals but can’t remember the last time you did.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy playing sax on the 19 bus, but no one noticed. Meanwhile, two pigeons were having a full-blown fight on the steps of the Civic Center station.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the quiet streets of Gràcia are always bustling. But at 3 PM on a Wednesday, it's like a ghost town, just the locals sipping café.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at how many times a single bus can be late. Locals either expect it or just walk.
